title: Adic proper adjunction comparison on the two constructible localizing presentations
statement:
Fix a universe $u$, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes in universe $u$, and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] of one of the families $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure convention [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal B_T\subset D_T$ be the bounded constructible object property of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with constructibility in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense [def-sfb-constructible-module], and let $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ use finite constant local models and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Form $\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ and $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal C_T)$ by [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure; sk-def-localizing-closure], in the same ordinary $D_T$ and with the same ambient coproducts indexed in universe $u+1$.

Then $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal C_T$ and $\mathcal L_T=\mathcal H_T$ as object properties in $D_T$. These identifications preserve the full inclusions into $D_T$ and the inclusions of the bounded subcategories into their hulls.

Let $F_g:\mathcal L_Z\to\mathcal L_Y$ be the canonical restriction of the actual ambient $Rg_*$ [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. Given a compact-support adjunction $a:Rg_!\dashv J$ on $\mathcal H_Z,\mathcal H_Y$ as in [sk-prop-sf-existence], the proper compactification comparison gives a natural isomorphism $e:Rg_!\xrightarrow{\sim}F_g$ under the displayed hull identifications. On $\mathcal L_Z,\mathcal L_Y$ it induces an adjunction $F_g\dashv J$ whose natural Hom bijection, for $M\in\mathcal L_Z$, $N\in\mathcal L_Y$ and $h:F_gM\to N$, is $h\longmapsto a_{M,N}(h\circ e_M)$. No derived-completeness condition is imposed.

proof.text: First verify the scheme hypotheses needed below. The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its underlying space is a point and its coordinate ring is Noetherian, since a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$. This uses the affine-cover definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure morphism of each $T=Z,Y$. Thus $T$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] it is also quasi-separated. In particular both the Noetherian constructibility comparison and the qcqs Tor-bound theorem apply, without assuming the base field algebraically closed.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian, and Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated.

proof.text: Eliminate the certificate [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate] into its three constructors. Each constructor specifies the actual condensed ring and its multiplication, so the results for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and the finite-subextension-valued $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ apply to this $\Lambda$, without changing scalar rings. By [lem-sfb-adic-constructibility-predicate-comparison], for each $T$ the property $\mathcal B_T$ is exactly $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ in the same $D_T$. If $K$ lies in this property with cohomology in $[a,b]$, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] gives Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b]$, hence $K\in\mathcal C_T$. Conversely $\mathcal C_T\subseteq\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ by the definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. These two inclusions prove $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal C_T$ as object properties, including integral torsion objects.

source.place: Clauses (1)-(2), applied after the ordinary constructibility comparison of the adic bullets in det-existence-restriction.proof.md.

proof.text: Expand the two intersection definitions [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure; sk-def-localizing-closure]. For any replete triangulated object property $P$ closed under the specified ambient coproducts, $\mathcal B_T\subseteq P$ if and only if $\mathcal C_T\subseteq P$, by step 2. The families being intersected are therefore identical, since both use $D_T$ and coproducts indexed in universe $u+1$. Hence $\mathcal L_T=\mathcal H_T$ pointwise. Identify the full subcategories by sending an object to that very same ambient object and every morphism to itself. Their ambient inclusions agree; the inclusions of the equal bounded classes into the equal hulls also agree on objects and morphisms. This is an equality of ordinary object properties, and introduces no derived-completeness condition.

source.place: Part (1), localizing categories; equality of their generating properties and identical full inclusions.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward], $F_g$ is the restriction of the actual ambient $Rg_*$ to $\mathcal L_Z,\mathcal L_Y$. Apply clause (1) of [det-cor-existence-ii-restriction] to the proper morphism $g$ and the admissible adic coefficient selected in step 2. It identifies the compact-support functor on $\mathcal H_Z,\mathcal H_Y$ with the restriction of that same ambient $Rg_*$. Under the identities of step 3 the latter restriction is $F_g$: its object and morphism maps agree, and its membership witnesses are properties. Thus the proper compactification comparison, restricted to these full subcategories, supplies $e:Rg_!\xrightarrow{\sim}F_g$. Its components are the ambient comparison components, now regarded as arrows of the full hull. Their inverses and naturality equations remain the same ambient arrows and equations.

source.place: Part (1): comparison with the identity compactification of a proper morphism.

proof.text: Regard the given adjunction $a:Rg_!\dashv J$ on the equal hulls from step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso] to $L=Rg_!$, $L\prime=F_g$, $R=J$ and the isomorphism $e$ of step 4. This gives $F_g\dashv J$ with Hom bijection $b_{M,N}(h)=a_{M,N}(h\circ e_M)$ for every $M,N$ in the hulls. Explicitly its inverse sends $q:M\to JN$ to $a_{M,N}^{-1}(q)\circ e_M^{-1}$. Both composites are identities by the inverse identities for $a_{M,N}$ and $e_M$; naturality follows from the naturality of $a$ and $e$. This applies to the supplied adjunction itself, with no replacement of its right adjoint and no completeness restriction.
